newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Former US rep sees Brazil coffee tree recovery.
newsitem.headline: Former US rep sees Brazil coffee tree recovery.

text.p: A majority of Brazilian coffee trees inspected in October and November by a former U.S. Department of Agriculture representative showed signs of good recovery from the 1994 frosts, the former official said

"In October and November I saw good recovery in the majority of trees hit by the 1994 frosts," Leon Yallouz told a coffee seminar. Yallouz visited coffee regions in the first field trip of his 1997/98 coffee estimate as a private consultant.
However, Yallouz did not make public his preliminary forecasts for the coming crop. He said he would be beginning a second field trip after the seminar ended January 22.
The government and producers have already said they expect a smaller harvest in 1997/98 than the previous crop estimated at 25 million bags.
